title: Queue Shepherding: Reservation Bands + Stepped Circuit Breaker for Regional Spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a queue shepherding system that combines reservation bands (time-windowed soft reservations), stepped circuit breakers, and regional spillover lanes to protect critical SLOs during bursty multi-region incidents. Aim: keep P90/P99 latency SLOs for premium tenants while providing predictable, explainable degradation for lower tiers and non-critical routes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic regional overload tests, premium tenant latency P99 increases by <20% and error rate stays <0.5% while best-effort routes are shed. 2) Circuit breaker transitions are observable and annotated in traces and Console dashboards. 3) Feature flag rollout completes without customer-facing errors. 4) Playbook for operators to manually trigger spillover and revert is documented.
design_notes: Core ideas: (a) Reservation bands: allocate time-sliced admission windows per priority band to guarantee micro-headroom for premium lanes; (b) Stepped circuit breaker: multiple thresholds (warn, degrade, cut) that trigger different actions—first trimming optional features (semantics-preserving slim-down), then moving requests to regional spillover lanes, finally rejecting or returning partial responses; (c) Regional spillover lanes: preference list of candidate regions and a lightweight ticketing protocol to avoid thundering herd; (d) Observability: expose per-tenant, per-route admissions, band occupancy, and circuit-breaker state with tags in traces.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Runtime admission API to register reservation bands and compute admission decisions (3 wks). Phase 2: Implement stepped circuit-breaker hooks (warn/degrade/cut) and feature-trimming hooks (2 wks). Phase 3: Regional spillover negotiation and ticketing protocol + backoff (2 wks). Phase 4: Console dashboards, metrics, playbook, canary rollout (1 wk). Use feature flag 'queue-shepherding.v1' for staged rollout.
rollout_plan: Canary in staging -> 10% tokenized traffic in us-west -> 50% region-local traffic -> enable cross-region spillover for non-premium only -> full rollout. Canary includes synthetic burst tests and A/B of admission decisions. Rollback via feature flag or operator kill switch.
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and circuit-breaker state machine. Integration test harness to replay real QPS patterns from last 90 days with injected region outage. Chaos test: force one region to fail and validate spillover/tokens backpressure. Load test with tenant-mix matching production (15% premium, 65% standard, 20% best-effort).
metrics: Expose: admission_decisions{band,route,tenant_tier}, band_occupancy{band,region}, circuit_breaker_state{route,region}, dropped_requests{reason,tenant_tier}, trimmed_features_rate{route}. Create SLO dashboards: latency_p90/p99_by_tier and error_rate_by_tier with alerts for regressions.
comments: 2026-02-11: Initial RFC posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RR/Queue+Shepherding+RFC (design sketches + state machine diagrams).

2026-02-18: Architecture review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to reuse the existing admission hook interface from runtime-1.18 to reduce surface area; Marcelo volunteered to prototype the band allocator. Action: Marcelo to submit prototype PR.

2026-02-26: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 — implements band allocator and admission API. Unit tests added. Initial microbench shows ~1.2% p99 overhead on the admission path.
2026-03-02: Design decision: use stepped circuit-breaker (three states) rather than binary to allow progressive degradation. Added acceptance criteria to limit premium P99 impact.

2026-03-05: Integration harness results: synthetic regional outage test passed for admission logic; however spillover ticketing showed increased latency due to DNS resolution retries. Action: add sticky region hints and aggressive connection reuse.
2026-03-10: Console dashboard mockups reviewed by PM and Design (link to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/ShepherdDash). Minor UI adjustments requested to surface tenant bands and current occupancy.
2026-03-12: Ready for canary deployment in us-west staging. Marcelo to coordinate canary window and notify on-call SREs. Next update after canary run and smoke tests.
